chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn al-Ash'ari, who said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Kaysan, from Musa ibn Salam, who said:

Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) performed the 'Umra. When he bid farewell to the House and arrived at the Bab al-Hannatin to exit from it, he stood in the courtyard of the mosque behind the Kaaba. Then he raised his hands and supplicated. Then he turned to us and said: 'The best place to seek fulfillment of needs is prayer in it; prayer in it is superior to prayer elsewhere by sixty years or sixty months.' When he arrived at the door, he said: 'O God, I have gone forth with the conviction that there is no god but You.'

key_terms.بَابِ الْحَنَّاطِينَ: Bab al-Hannatin (a specific gate of the Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of praying behind the Kaaba according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) emphasizes the superior spiritual merit of praying in the courtyard of the Kaaba, specifically behind it, stating that prayer there is equivalent to sixty years or months of prayer elsewhere. This narration, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, underscores the sanctity of the Mataf area and the Kaaba's role as a focal point for divine connection. The Imam’s concluding supplication, 'O Allah, I have gone out on the basis that there is no god but You,' reflects the essence of Tawhid and the pilgrim's departure with a purified state of heart.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 30-42 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Kaysan, on the authority of Musa ibn Salam, “

When Abul Hassan Al-Ridha (s) performed the ‘Umra (minor) Hajj pilgrimage, he (s) said farewell to the House (of God). He went to the ‘Babul al-Hannatin  and stood up in the mosque behind the Kaaba. He raised up his hands to pray and told us, ‘This is the best location in which one can ask God to fulfill his requests. Saying prayers here is worth praying for sixty months or sixty years elsewhere.’ When he approached the door he said, ‘I will leave with the belief that there is no god but Thee.’”
